papers.abstract: Humanoid robots have the potential to automate a wide range of physical tasks. Progress toward generalist humanoid autonomy, however, remains constrained by a data bottleneck: mapping pixels and free-form language to low-level joint commands requires paired supervision, and no corpus of such data exists at sufficiently large scale. Some approaches rely on human teleoperation and wearable capture devices, which require at least an hour of human time to produce an hour of data. We present HALO, a humanoid autonomy system powered by a pipeline that synthesizes vision-language-motion data across a thousand procedurally generated homes. The corpus scales with compute rather than human labor. papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remain prone to visual hallucinations when correct responses depend on subtle visual details. One line of post-training methods constructs visual contrasts through image retrieval, generation, or editing to improve fine-grained perception. However, these contrasts are not built around the model's own hallucinations, making it difficult to ensure that supervision targets its actual perceptual confusions. Another line suppresses hallucinated outputs through response correction or preference learning under fixed image conditions, but leaves the design of supervision signals on the image-input side underexplored. alternate_titles: GRAIL 2026: Workshop on Generative, Retrieval-augmented, and Agentic Intelligence for Personalization
papers.abstract: Personalization is being rebuilt around generative models. Large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, and agentic systems now shape how recommenders retrieve, rank, explain, converse, and even simulate users—yet they also surface hard problems of hallucination, control, evaluation, privacy, and fairness. GRAIL 2026 brings together academic researchers and industry practitioners to advance generative, retrieval-augmented, and agentic approaches to recommendation—including LLM-based retrieval and ranking, retrieval-augmented and knowledge-grounded personalization, conversational and agentic recommenders, multimodal content generation, user simulation, and synthetic data—while giving equal attention to these open challenges and their long-term user impact.

In this article, we argue that GenAI can bridge the persistent gap between optimization's technical capabilities and its limited real-world uptake. Insight establishes a trusted, up-to-date view of current operations; Interpretability explains model logic and trade-offs; Interactivity enables conversational what-if analysis; Improvisation supports model updates and event-driven re-optimization. alternate_titles: MUSE: A Simple Yet Effective Multimodal Search-Based Framework for Lifelong User Interest Modeling
papers.abstract: Lifelong user interest modeling is crucial for industrial recommender systems, yet existing approaches rely predominantly on ID-based features, suffering from poor generalization on long-tail items and limited semantic expressiveness. While recent work explores multimodal representations for behavior retrieval in the General Search Unit (GSU), they often neglect multimodal integration in the fine-grained modeling stage---the Exact Search Unit (ESU). In this work, we present a systematic analysis of how to effectively leverage multimodal signals across both stages of the two-stage lifelong modeling framework. Our key insight is that simplicity suffices in the GSU: lightweight cosine similarity with high-quality multimodal embeddings outperforms complex retrieval mechanisms. papers.abstract: Recent work leverages large-scale pretrained foundation models (FMs) to transfer generalizable representations to downstream advertising tasks. Most existing paradigms transfer user representations (URs) and item representations (IRs), while underutilizing the user-item cross representations (CRs) generated by deeper interaction layers. Although a recent approach transfers target-aware embeddings (TAEs), it requires real-time upstream FM inference alongside downstream model inference, introducing additional engineering complexity and overhead. To address these limitations, we propose Large Foundation Model for Ads Recommendation (LFM4Ads), an efficient pretrain-then-transfer framework for cross-domain ad recommendation. papers.abstract: Traditional ID-based recommender systems often struggle with cold-start and generalization challenges. Multimodal recommendation systems, which leverage textual and visual data, offer a promising solution to mitigate these issues. However, existing industrial approaches typically adopt a two-stage training paradigm: first pretraining a multimodal model, then applying its frozen representations to train the recommendation model. This decoupled framework suffers from misalignment between multimodal learning and recommendation objectives, as well as an inability to adapt dynamically to new data. To address these limitations, we propose LEMUR, the first large-scale multimodal recommender system trained end-to-end from raw data. papers.abstract: Click-through rate (CTR) models estimate the probability of a user clicking on an item and exhibit varying prediction reliability across instances at inference time. papers.abstract: LLM-based applications increasingly rely on models served through third-party providers, where the model's own alignment is often the sole defense against misuse. In this regime, developers must implement both red-teaming and guardrails themselves, yet existing in-context methods address these objectives in isolation and do not refine demonstrations against the target LLM's responses. We propose TrojanShot, a unified framework that post-trains a demonstration generator via reinforcement learning to produce potent in-context examples for both attack (Trojan shots) and defense (Guardian shots), operating entirely at the prompt layer of the target LLM. Our iterative route encodes all traits as G profile features in one ranker rather than learning or serving G factor models. An offline module probes the ranker to construct an additive surrogate for profile updates across neural and tree rankers. papers.abstract: Recent advances in Generative AI (GenAI) have enabled strong capabilities in language understanding, content generation, vision-language reasoning, and multimodal interaction. However, most existing benchmarks emphasize general-purpose reasoning and task performance, offering limited evaluation of whether AI systems can accurately understand, represent, retrieve, and generate culturally grounded knowledge across diverse communities and social contexts. This limitation restricts the reliable deployment of GenAI in high-impact domains such as education, healthcare, and public services. alternate_titles: Process In-Context Learning: Confusion-Aware Demonstration Retrieval and Dynamic Insertion for Mathematical Reasoning
papers.abstract: In-context learning (ICL) has achieved strong results across a wide range of large language model (LLM) tasks. However, its effectiveness for problems that require step-by-step deduction, such as mathematical reasoning, is still not well understood. One major limitation of existing ICL methods is that demonstrations are chosen before inference and remain unchanged throughout reasoning. As a result, they cannot respond to confusion points that emerge during multi-step problem solving, such as uncertain calculations or missing logical transitions. When these confusion points are not resolved, they may propagate and ultimately degrade answer accuracy. alternate_titles: Privacy-Aware Representation Decoupling in Federated Recommendation against Attribute Inference Attacks
papers.abstract: Federated recommender systems (FedRec) aim to preserve user privacy by keeping sensitive data on client devices and sharing only model parameters with a central server. However, FedRec is still vulnerable to attribute inference attacks (AIAs), where server-side adversaries exploit uploaded parameters to infer users' private attributes. Existing FedRec approaches face a suboptimal privacy-performance trade-off. Privacy-focused methods mask attribute-related features in representations to protect sensitive information, but degrade recommendation accuracy. In contrast, performance-focused methods preserve accuracy by retaining these features but risk privacy leakage through uploaded representations. Traditional sketches often use large, fixed-size counters, leading to inefficient memory usage in skewed data distributions. Recent solutions, such as hierarchical structures and dynamic counters, attempt to improve memory efficiency but struggle to balance this with detection accuracy. In this work, we present Nino-Sketch, a memory-efficient and versatile sketch for data stream analysis. Recent work mitigates this via two reasoning paradigms: reason-then-generate, which refines intermediate states before producing the draft, and reason-while-generating, which interleaves reasoning with token generation. papers.title: LLMJudge: Meta-Evaluating Automatic Relevance Judgments
alternate_titles: LLMJudge: Meta-Evaluating Automatic Relevance Judgments
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to produce the relevance labels that underpin the evaluation of information retrieval (IR) and retrieval-augmented generation systems. Yet delegating relevance assessment to an LLM raises a meta-evaluation question that is hard to answer with existing resources: when, and how much, can we trust an automatic judge? We present LLMJudge, a resource for meta-evaluating LLM-generated relevance judgments. LLMJudge collects 42 complete judgment sets over the TREC 2023 Deep Learning track, spanning fine-tuned, proprietary, and open-source models and a wide range of prompting strategies. alternate_titles: LIFT: A Learning-aware Intervention Framework for Cold-Start Recommendation on TikTok Live
papers.abstract: On billion-scale live streaming platforms such as TikTok, a core challenge is to distribute millions of newly initiated live streams to potential viewers. The ephemerality and real-time variability of live streams demand an aggressive and dynamic cold-start strategy to capture value within an extremely limited window. Beyond this temporal urgency, the system faces a unique challenge: a two-way interactive feedback loop in which recommendations directly influence streamer behavior and subsequent viewer feedback. Traditional methods, however, lack the ability to intervene at critical learning moments and fail to provide the active incentives needed to optimize the streamer-user feedback loop. papers.abstract: Knowledge Graphs (KGs) are foundational infrastructure for search, question answering, and entity-centric applications, on the open web and within domain-specific platforms. We first frame KG construction and the open challenges that arise when facts are extracted from noisy, evolving sources. alternate_titles: IDs That Mean Something: A Hands-On Tutorial on Semantic IDs for Recommender Systems
papers.abstract: Traditional recommender systems rely on arbitrary integer IDs to identify items, which carry no semantic information and force models to learn representations from interaction data. While leveraging content information can partially mitigate cold-start, this paradigm inherently suffers from exploding embedding tables and scenario-specific architectures. Recent years have seen the emergence of semantic IDs, which encode semantic information directly into the item identity, reflecting content, hierarchy, and relationships. This framework addresses the above limitations by offering a principled way to encode large-scale semantic information into item identity, benefiting both generative and discriminative applications and unlocking more native unification across modalities, domains, and tasks. papers.title: GraphMind: From Operational Traces to Self-Evolving Workflow Automation
alternate_titles: GraphMind: From Operational Traces to Self-Evolving Workflow Automation
papers.abstract: Complex operational workflows are central to system operations, yet remain difficult to automate due to heavy human input and limited adaptability. We present GraphMind, a system that constructs, executes, and evolves action-centric workflow graphs with minimal human effort. The system operates in three phases. First, a scalable offline pipeline extracts structured workflow graphs from human resolution traces, capturing problems, actions, and their causal relationships.
